samples.summary: `slides export` (PPTX) has no per-image tolerance, so the new SSRF guard turns a previously-working image into a total export failure
samples.evidence: The change deliberately makes a refused/unreachable image an ordinary outcome and patches both docs paths for it (`pdf-image-painter.ts:99-101` catches and reports; `docx-exporter.ts:448-455` records a failed entry). The slides path was not patched: `packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:209` builds the same guarded `createImageFetcher`, `packages/cli/src/slides/pptx-export.ts:14` awaits it unguarded, and `exportPptx` calls `await opts.fetchImage(src)` at `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/index.ts:162` with no try/catch. Any deck whose image `src` names a non-public host that is not the configured server (an internal MinIO/blob host that used to be fetched fine, a stale intranet URL, or a name whose DNS lookup fails) now rejects and the whole `slides export deck.pptx` aborts through `outputError`, where before this change the image was fetched and embedded.

samples.summary: Address-pinning plain-`http:` image fetches sends `Host: <ip>` on Node, breaking name-based virtual hosts that worked before
samples.evidence: `pinnedUrls` (line 396-404) rewrites every `http:` target's hostname to a resolved IP, and `dialOnce` tries to compensate with `headers: { host }` (line 491). The code's own comment at 476-480 states Node's undici drops `host` as a forbidden header name, so the request really arrives as `Host: <ip>`. Any public image served over plain http from a shared/vhosted origin (very common for CDNs and reverse proxies) will now get the wrong site or a 404 instead of the image. Combined with the new silent-drop behaviour in the docx/pdf exporters, the image just disappears from the export with only a `console.warn`. This is a behaviour regression on a path that worked before the change.

samples.summary: Response bodies are left undrained on the error and declared-too-large paths, the exact leak the redirect path guards against
samples.evidence: Line 540 cancels a redirect body with the comment "an unread one holds its socket open until the agent times out". The same reasoning applies at line 530-534, where a non-ok response is thrown on with `res.body` never read or cancelled, and at `readCappedBlob` line 577 (`if (... declared > maxBytes) throw tooLarge();`) which throws before touching `res.body` — while the streaming branch at line 592 does cancel. Because failed images no longer abort the export (docx/pdf now swallow them), a document with many 404 or oversize images accumulates undrained bodies for the lifetime of the export.

samples.summary: `assertResolvedHostIsPublic` passes (fail-open) when the resolver returns an empty address list
samples.evidence: After `addresses = await lookup(host)`, `addresses.find(isPrivateHost)` on `[]` is `undefined`, so the function returns `[]` — indistinguishable from the "exempt host, nothing to pin" result. `pinnedUrls(target, [])` then returns the unpinned name and the fetch proceeds with no address ever having been validated. The doc comment claims a name that cannot be checked is refused; an empty resolver answer is exactly that case and is not refused. The default `dns.lookup` will usually throw instead, but an injected/alternate resolver, or a resolver returning an empty record set, silently skips the check.

samples.summary: `assertNoDotSegments` misses the percent-encoded dot-segment spellings the WHATWG URL parser also resolves
samples.evidence: The backstop only compares each segment to the literal `'.'` and `'..'`. Per the URL spec a "double-dot path segment" is `..`, `.%2e`, `%2e.` or `%2e%2e` (case-insensitive), and `new URL('http://h/a/%2e%2e/b').pathname` is `/b`. A future call site that hands `printDryRun` a raw `%2e%2e` — precisely the "forgetful caller" case this guard exists for, per its own doc comment — would print a walked-up URL as "the request that would be sent". `seg()` itself is safe (it percent-encodes the `%`), so only the backstop is incomplete.

samples.summary: Swallowing per-image failures also silences them in the browser exporters, where `console.warn` is invisible to the user
samples.evidence: `collectAndEmbedImages` now defaults `onImageError` to `warnImageError` (console.warn) and `DocxExporter.collectImages` hard-codes `console.warn` at `packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:452`. Both exporters are shared with the frontend (PdfExporter/DocxExporter are used from the browser app), so a browser-side export of a document whose image host is unreachable now silently produces a PDF/DOCX with missing images and no UI signal, where previously the export rejected and the caller could surface a toast. The DOCX path has no reporter seam at all — the CLI-motivated policy is baked into a shared package.

samples.summary: The per-image time bound multiplies across dial attempts and redirect hops
samples.evidence: `AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs)` is created fresh per dial inside `dialOnce`'s loop (up to `MAX_DIAL_ADDRESSES` = 4) and again for every redirect hop (up to `MAX_IMAGE_REDIRECTS` = 5, i.e. 6 requests). With the 30 s default a single image can consume roughly 4 x 6 x 30 s = 12 minutes of wall clock, and a document with many such images multiplies that again, despite the doc comment claiming "every hop is also bounded" as the fix for an export that would otherwise hang.

samples.summary: `clampUpstreamText` discards any legitimate message that happens to begin with `<`
samples.evidence: `if (!trimmed || trimmed.startsWith('<')) return null;` is meant to reject HTML documents, but it also drops a real backend message such as `<title> must not be empty` or `<id> is required`, replacing it with a bare `HTTP 400` (via `upstreamMessage`) or, on the envelope path (line 165), with `HTTP <status>` — losing exactly the text the rest of this change went to trouble to preserve.

samples.summary: `seg` can now throw synchronously from a render-path helper
samples.evidence: `fileUrl(documentId)` is a plain synchronous helper called while building UI (it returns a URL string, not a promise), and it now calls `seg(documentId)` which throws `Invalid path segment` for `.` / `..`. A document id of `.` or `..` (from a crafted route param, since react-router percent-decodes params) turns a 404-worthy request into a thrown exception during render rather than a handled fetch failure. Same shape applies to the other synchronous non-async `seg` call sites.

finding.summary: `slides export` (PPTX) has no per-image tolerance, so the new SSRF guard turns a previously-working image into a total export failure
finding.evidence: The change deliberately makes a refused/unreachable image an ordinary outcome and patches both docs paths for it (`pdf-image-painter.ts:99-101` catches and reports; `docx-exporter.ts:448-455` records a failed entry). The slides path was not patched: `packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:209` builds the same guarded `createImageFetcher`, `packages/cli/src/slides/pptx-export.ts:14` awaits it unguarded, and `exportPptx` calls `await opts.fetchImage(src)` at `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/index.ts:162` with no try/catch. Any deck whose image `src` names a non-public host that is not the configured server (an internal MinIO/blob host that used to be fetched fine, a stale intranet URL, or a name whose DNS lookup fails) now rejects and the whole `slides export deck.pptx` aborts through `outputError`, where before this change the image was fetched and embedded.

verdict.reason: Every cited location checks out. `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/index.ts:162` does `const { bytes, mime } = await opts.fetchImage(src);` inside the dedup loop with no try/catch and no skip path, so a single rejection aborts the whole archive build. The CLI adapter `packages/cli/src/slides/pptx-export.ts:12-17` awaits the injected fetcher unguarded, and `packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:209-210` injects the guarded `createImageFetcher` with only `serverBase` (no allowedHosts override); the surrounding try/catch at slides.ts:212-213 merely funnels the failure into `outputError`, i.e. the whole `slides export` fails, which is the reported symptom rather than a mitigation. The guard genuinely throws on real inputs: `packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:286-291` refuses a non-public host that is neither the configured server nor listed in WAFFLEBASE_IMAGE_HOSTS, and `:347-364` refuses a name that fails to resolve or resolves to a private address; `createImageFetcher` runs both via `guard()` at `:451-460` on the first hop and each redirect. The asymmetry the finding rests on is also real: `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-image-painter.ts:99-101` catches per image and reports via `onImageError`, and `packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:441-455` explicitly catches, warns, and records a failed entry so 'one unreachable or refused image must not cost the whole export'. No caller-side or model-side filter restricts slide image srcs to same-origin/data URLs, so the refusal path is reachable. Impact is an all-or-nothing export failure on a previously working deck — a real correctness/error-handling defect in this lens's lane. No refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: Address-pinning plain-`http:` image fetches sends `Host: <ip>` on Node, breaking name-based virtual hosts that worked before
finding.evidence: `pinnedUrls` (line 396-404) rewrites every `http:` target's hostname to a resolved IP, and `dialOnce` tries to compensate with `headers: { host }` (line 491). The code's own comment at 476-480 states Node's undici drops `host` as a forbidden header name, so the request really arrives as `Host: <ip>`. Any public image served over plain http from a shared/vhosted origin (very common for CDNs and reverse proxies) will now get the wrong site or a 404 instead of the image. Combined with the new silent-drop behaviour in the docx/pdf exporters, the image just disappears from the export with only a `console.warn`. This is a behaviour regression on a path that worked before the change.

verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as described. `pinnedUrls` (image-fetcher.ts:396-404) rewrites the hostname of every non-exempt `http:` target to a resolved IP address, and `dialOnce` (image-fetcher.ts:470-499) attempts to compensate via `headers: { host }` at line 491 only for pinned dials. The code's own comment at lines 476-483 states that undici drops `host` as a forbidden header name, so on Node the request arrives as `Host: <ip>`; docs/design/cli.md:1185-1192 records the same as a "Known limitation" and docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-lessons.md:140 notes it was empirically verified on Node 22. No guard prevents plain-`http:` public image URLs from reaching this path: assertFetchableImageUrl (line 280) allows `http`, and only exempt hosts skip resolution/pinning (assertResolvedHostIsPublic:338-345). Impact is amplified because a failed image fetch is non-fatal and the image is dropped from the export with only a stderr report (docs/design/cli.md:1198-1208). Real behavior regression on a reachable path; being an intentional, documented trade-off does not eliminate the runtime defect under the correctness rubric.

finding.summary: `pinnedUrl` dials only `addresses[0]`, discarding fetch's multi-address (happy-eyeballs) fallback — http image fetches can fail on hosts whose first record is unreachable
finding.evidence: `const address = addresses[0]; url.hostname = ...` uses the first record from `dnsLookup(hostname, { all: true, verbatim: true })`. `verbatim: true` preserves resolver order, which for a dual-stack CDN commonly puts the AAAA record first. On a machine without working IPv6 (or when the first A record is down), the normal `fetch(name)` path would try the remaining addresses; the pinned URL cannot, so the connection fails and — combined with the new swallow in the exporters — the image is silently dropped from the export. No fallback loop over the other approved addresses exists.

verdict.reason: The finding describes a `pinnedUrl` that collapses the approved address set to `addresses[0]` with "no fallback loop". That code is not in this tree. `pinnedUrls` (image-fetcher.ts:396-404) maps EVERY approved address (capped at MAX_DIAL_ADDRESSES=4, line 374) to its own dial URL; `assertResolvedHostIsPublic` returns the full address list (line 365); and `dialOnce` (lines 470-499) walks `dials` in order, catching connect-level failures and advancing to the next address, rethrowing only timeouts (isTimeout, 415-418) and finally `throw lastError`. The redirect loop re-derives the full dial list per hop (lines 503, 511, 550), so fallback persists across redirects. Tests at test/image-fetcher.test.ts:804-844 assert the exact happy-eyeballs fallback the finding says is missing (seen === ['http://93.184.216.34/a.png','http://203.0.113.7/a.png']). Grep for `addresses[0]` finds no source occurrence — only a test comment and a task-doc note (docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-lessons.md:121-122) recording this as an already-corrected past defect, which is the likely source of the reviewer's quoted evidence. Since the premise is absent, the dependent claim about the exporter swallow silently dropping the image also does not follow.
